questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Although $+3$ oxidation state is most common in lanthanoids, cerium still shows $+4$ oxidation state because :
options: After losing one more electron, it acquires $4f^{14}$ electronic configuration.
Its nearest inert gas is Radon.
After losing one more electron, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Cerium (Ce) is $58$.

The electronic configuration of Ce is $[Xe] 4f^{1} 5d^{1} 6s^{2}$.

In $+3$ oxidation state, the electronic configuration of $Ce^{3+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{1}$.

By losing one more electron, it forms $Ce^{4+}$ ion.

The electronic configuration of $Ce^{4+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{0}$, which is a highly stable noble gas configuration.

Thus, Cerium shows $+4$ oxidation state because after losing one more electron from $+3$ state, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.

Answer: After losing one more electron, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The lanthanide ion having four unpaired electrons is
(Given : Atomic numbers of Ce $=58$, Nd $=60$, Tb $=65$ and Ho $=67$)
questions.solution:
The general electronic configuration of lanthanide ions $\text{Ln}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{Z-57}$, where $Z$ is the atomic number.

For $\text{Ho}^{3+}$ ($Z=67$):
Number of $4f$ electrons $= 67 - 57 = 10$
Configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{10}$.
Since the $f$-subshell has 7 orbitals, 10 electrons will fill as 3 pairs and 4 unpaired electrons. Number of unpaired electrons $= 14 - 10 = 4$.

For $\text{Nd}^{3+}$ ($Z=60$):
Number of $4f$ electrons $= 60 - 57 = 3$
Configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{3}$.
Number of unpaired electrons $= 3$.

For $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ ($Z=58$):
Number of $4f$ electrons $= 58 - 57 = 1$
Configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{1}$.
Number of unpaired electrons $= 1$.

For $\text{Tb}^{3+}$ ($Z=65$):
Number of $4f$ electrons $= 65 - 57 = 8$
Configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{8}$.
Number of unpaired electrons $= 14 - 8 = 6$.

Thus, $\text{Ho}^{3+}$ has exactly four unpaired electrons.

Answer: $\text{Ho}^{3+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The green paramagnetic species formed by heating KMnO$_4$ at $513$ K is
questions.solution:
When potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) is heated at $513\text{ K}$, it decomposes to form potassium manganate, manganese dioxide, and oxygen gas.

$2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{513\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

The species $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ (potassium manganate) is green in color.

In $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$, the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ is $+6$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{6+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$.

Since it contains one unpaired electron in the $d$-orbital, it is paramagnetic in nature.

Thus, the green paramagnetic species formed is $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$.

Answer: $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $\text{Ti}^{2+}\ (3d^2)$ is :
questions.solution:
The atomic number of $\text{Ti}$ is $22$.

Electronic configuration of $\text{Ti}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^2 4s^2$.

Electronic configuration of $\text{Ti}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^2$.

Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 2$.

Spin-only magnetic moment, $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

$\mu = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $2.84$ BM

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Transition metal/compound/complex)List II (Catalytic Role)
A. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$I. Preparation of ammonia from $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ mixture
B. $\text{Fe}$II. Polymerisation of alkynes
C. $\text{PdCl}_2$III. Preparation of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ from $\text{SO}_2$
D. Ni complexIV. Oxidation of ethyne to ethanal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is used as a catalyst in the Contact process for the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ during the preparation of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Thus, A matches with III.

Finely divided $\text{Fe}$ is used as a catalyst in the Haber process for the preparation of ammonia from $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{H}_2$ mixture. Thus, B matches with I.

$\text{PdCl}_2$ is used as a catalyst in the Wacker process for the oxidation of ethene (referred to as ethyne in the given options) to ethanal. Thus, C matches with IV.

$\text{Ni}$ complexes are used as catalysts for the polymerisation of alkynes (e.g., polymerisation of ethyne to cyclooctatetraene). Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) :
Ionisation enthalpies of early actinoids are lower than for early lanthanoids.
Reason (R) :
Electrons are entering $5 f$ orbitals in actinoids which experience greater shielding from nuclear charge.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$.
Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true but $(\mathbf{R})$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$.
questions.solution: Ionisation enthalpies of early actinoids are lower than early lanthanoids. This is because $5 f$ orbitals will penetrate less into the inner core of electrons. The $5 f$ electrons, will be more effectively shielded from the nuclear charge than the $4 f$ electrons of corresponding lanthanoids.

questions.q: The stability of ${Cu}^{2 +}$ is more than ${Cu}^{+}$ salts in aqueous solution due to -

The ${Cu}^{2 +}$ ion has a greater charge density than ${Cu}^{+}$ ion and thus forms much stronger bonds releasing more hydration energy.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?

A. All the transition metals except scandium form $MO$ oxides which are ionic.
B. The highest oxidation number corresponding to the group number in transition metal oxides is attained in ${Sc}_{2}{O}_{3}$ to ${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$ .
C. Basic character increases from ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}to{V}_{2}{O}_{4}to{V}_{2}{O}_{5}$.
D. ${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$ dissolves in acids to give ${VO}_{4}^{- 3}$ salts.
E. $CrO$ is basic but ${Cr}_{2}{O}_{3}$ is amphoteric.

questions.solution:
Lower oxidation state oxides are ionic. The highest oxidation number in the oxides, coincides with the group number and is attained in ${Sc}_{2}{O}_{3}$ to ${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$. The structure of ${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$ is more covalent than that of ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$ and ${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$, which makes it more acidic. As a result, the basicity of ${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$ is greater than that of ${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$, which is in turn greater than that of ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$.

Here in option C they have gien the increasing order of acidic character. So Option C is wrong.

${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$ dissolves in acids to give ${{VO}_{2}}^{+}$ not in ${VO}_{4}^{- 3}$ salts. So Option D is also wrong. Lower oxides are basic oxides and all chromium oxides other than $CrO$ are amphoteric oxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : Generally, $3d$ transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R : Involvement of $3d$-electrons in addition to $4s$-electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: $\text{A}$ is not correct but $\text{R}$ is correct.
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$.
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\text{A}$.
$\text{A}$ is correct but $\text{R}$ is not correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion A is correct because transition metals generally have high melting points due to strong metallic bonding.

Reason R is correct and explains Assertion A because the strong metallic bonding in $3d$ transition metals is attributed to the involvement of a greater number of electrons from the $3d$ subshell in addition to the $4s$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.

Thus, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$.

questions.q: Because of lanthanoid contraction, which of the following pairs of elements have nearly the same atomic radii? (Number in the parenthesis are atomic numbers).
questions.solution:
$Zr\left(40\right)$ and $Hf\left(72\right)$: Because of the lanthanoid contraction, $Zr$ (atomic radii $160$ pm) and $Hf$ (atomic radii $158$ pm) have nearly the same atomic radii.

Lanthanoids include the elements from lanthanum $La\left(Z = 57\right) to lutetium $Lu $\left(Z = 71\right)$. Zirconium $Zr\left(40\right) belong$ to $the second transition series \left(4d\right) and Hf\left(72\right) belongs to the third transition series \left(5d\right). Lanthanoid contraction is related to the intervention of the$4f -$orbitals, which are filled before the $5d -$series of elements start. The filling of $4f$, if orbitals before $5d -orbitals result in a regular decrease in atomic radii, which compensates the expected increases in atomic size with increasing atomic number. As a result of lanthanoid contraction, the elements of second and third transition series have almost similar atomic radii.

questions.q:
Which of the following lanthanoid ions is diamagnetic?
(At. nos. $\mathrm{Ce}=58, \mathrm{Sm}=62, \mathrm{Eu}=63$, $\mathrm{Yb}=70$ )
questions.solution:
Lanthanoid ion with no unpaired electron is diamagnetic in nature.
$\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm{Ce}_{58} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^2 5 d^0 6 s^2 \\
C e^{2+} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^2 \quad \text{ (two unpaired electrons) }
\end{array}$
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{Sm}_{62} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^6 5 d^0 6 s^2 \\
\mathrm{Sm}^{2+} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^6 \quad(s i x \text{ unpaired electrons) } \\
\mathrm{Eu}_{63} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^7 5 d^0 6 s^2 \\
\mathrm{Eu}^{2+} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^7 \quad \text{ (seven unpaired electrons) } \\
\mathrm{Yb}_{70} & =\left[\mathrm{X}_e\right] 4 f^{14} 5 d^0 6 s^2 \\
\mathrm{Yb}^{2+} & =[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 f^{14} \quad \text{ (no unpaired electrons) }
\end{aligned}$
Because of the absence of unpaired electrons, $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$ is diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following complex ions is not expected to absorb visible light?
questions.solution: Key Idea For the absorption of visible light, presence of unpaired d-electrons is the necessity. (a) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}, \mathrm{Ni}$ is present as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$. $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]$3 $\mathrm{~d}^$8 4 $\mathrm{~s}^$0 $$ \\ (Pairing occurs because $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$is a strong field ligand). Since, in $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$, no unpaired electron is present in d-orbitals, it does not absorb visible light. (b) In $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}, \mathrm{Cr}$ is present as $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$. $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^3 4 \mathrm{~s}^0$ (Three unpaired electrons) (c) In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}, \mathrm{Fe}$ is present as $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$. $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^6 4 \mathrm{~s}^0$ (Four unpaired electrons) (d) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Ni}$ is present as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$. $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^8 4 \mathrm{~s}^0$ (Two unpaired electrons) The complexes given in option (b), (c), (d) have unpaired electrons, thus absorb visible light.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the elements with the following outer orbital configurations may exhibit the largest number of oxidation states ?
questions.solution:
Key Idea Number of oxidation states exhibited by d-block elements is the sum of number of electrons (unpaired) in d-orbitals and number of electrons in s-orbital.
(a) $3 \mathrm{~d}^3, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=3+2=5$
(b) $3 \mathrm{~d}^5, 4 \mathrm{~s}^1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=5+1=6$
(c) $3 \mathrm{~d}^5, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=5+2=7$
(d) $3 \mathrm{~d}^2, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=2+2=4$
Hence, element with $3 \mathrm{~d}^5, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2$ configuration exhibits largest number of oxidation states.
questions.question: Which one of the elements with the following outer orbital configurations may exhibit the largest number of oxidation states ?
questions.explanation:
Key Idea Number of oxidation states exhibited by d-block elements is the sum of number of electrons (unpaired) in d-orbitals and number of electrons in s-orbital.
(a) $3 \mathrm{~d}^3, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=3+2=5$
(b) $3 \mathrm{~d}^5, 4 \mathrm{~s}^1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=5+1=6$
(c) $3 \mathrm{~d}^5, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=5+2=7$
(d) $3 \mathrm{~d}^2, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=2+2=4$
Hence, element with $3 \mathrm{~d}^5, 4 \mathrm{~s}^2$ configuration exhibits largest number of oxidation states.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement among the following:
options: Lanthanoid contraction is the accumulation of successive shrinkages
As a result of lanthanoid contraction, the properties of $4 d$ series of the transition elements have no similarities with the $5 d$ series of elements
Shielding power of $4 f$ electrons is quite weak
Thee is a decrease in the radii of the atoms or ions as one proceeds from La to $\mathrm{Lu}$
questions.solution:
There is a steady decrease in the radii as the atomic number of the lanthanide elements increases. For every additional proton added in nucleus the corresponding electron goes to $4 f$ subshell. The shape of $f$-orbitals is very much diffused and they have poor shielding effect. The effective nuclear charge increases which causes the contraction in the size of electron charge cloud. This contraction in size is quite regular and known as Lanthanoid contraction. Since the change in the ionic radii in the lanthanide series is very small, thus their chemical properties are similar.
Related Theory There is no regular trend in ionization potential in the group due to lanthanide contraction. Caution The lanthanide contraction is responsible because $\mathrm{Zr}$ and Hf have about the same radius

questions.q:
Which one of the following ions is the most stable in aqueous solution?
(At No. $\mathrm{Ti}=22, \mathrm{~V}=23, \mathrm{Cr}=24, \mathrm{Mn}=$ 25)
questions.solution:
In aqueous solution the configuration of the ions are following
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}(21) & =3 d^3 4 s^0 \Rightarrow t_{2 g}{ }^3 e_g^0 \\
\mathrm{ V}^{3+}(20) & =3 d^2 4 s^0 \Rightarrow t_{28}{ }^2 e_g^0 \\
\mathrm{Tr}^{3+}(19) & =3 d^1 4 s^0 \Rightarrow t_{28}{ }^1 e_g^0 \\
\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}(22) & =3 d^4 4 s^0 \Rightarrow t_{2 g}{ }^4 e_g^0
\end{aligned}$
We know that half-filled and fully filled orbitals are more stable than partially filled orbitals. Hence among the given ions the only $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ ion which occupies half-filled $t_{2 g}$ orbitals.
Caution
Although $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ ion has half-filled $t_{\text{s orbital }}$ but there is one more electron filled in $e_R$ orbital which reduces the stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: More number of oxidation states are exhibited by the actinoids than by the lanthanoids. The main reason for this is:
options: more active nature of the actinoids
more energy difference between $5 f$ and $6 d$ orbitals than that between $4 f$ and $5 d$ orbitals
lesser energy difference between $5 f$ and $6 d$ orbitals than that between $4 f$ and $5 d$ orbitals
greater metallic character of the lanthanoids than that of the corresponding actinoids
questions.solution:
Actinides exhibit more number of oxidation states than lanthanides because of lesser energy difference between the $5 f$ and $6 d$ orbitals than that between the $4 f$ and $5 d$ orbitals.
Related Theory
Actinides have a very small energy gap between $5 f$ and $6 d$ orbitals, so they can easily form a variety of configurations and hence they are found to be stable in various oxidation states. Lanthanides are comparatively less electropositive than actinides and due to that reason, they are less reactive than actinides.

questions.solution:
Metal ions having variable oxidation number can form more than one types of binary compound. Fe shows $+2,+3$ oxidation states. Thus, it can form $\mathrm{FeCl}_3, \mathrm{FeCl}_2$.
Related Theory
Binary compounds are chemical compounds comprising of two distinct elements. For example, water, calcium chloride etc.

$\mathrm{Zn}$, even being a transition metal shows only +2 oxidation state, due to fully filled $3 d$ subshell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lanthanoids are:
options: 14 elements in the sixth period (atomic no. 90 to 103) that filling of $4 f$ sublevel
14 element in the seventh period (atomic number $=90$ to 103 ) that are filling $5 f$ sublevel
14 element in the sixth period (atomic number $=58$ to 71 ) that are filling the $4 f$ sublevel
14 elements in the seventh period (atomic number $=50$ to 71 ) that are filling $4 f$ sublevel
questions.solution:
The elements in which the additional electrons enters $(n-2) f$ orbitals are called inner transition elements. $4 f$-block elements are also called lanthanides or rare earths so lanthanides are 14 elements in the sixth period (atomic no. $=58$ to 71 ) that are filling $4 f$-sublevel.
Related Theory
Lanthanoid contraction effect results from poor shielding of nuclear charge (nuclear attractive force on electrons) by 4 felectrons so effective nuclear charge increases; the $6 s$ electrons are drawn towards the nucleus, thus resulting in a smaller atomic radius.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following characteristics of the transition metals is associated with their catalytic activity?
questions.solution:
Transition elements are elements that have partially filled d-orbitals. These elements show variable oxidation state because their valence electrons in two different sets of orbitals, that is (n-1)d and $\mathrm{ns}$. The energy difference between these orbitals is very less, so both the energy levels can be used for bond formation. Thus, transition elements have variable oxidation states.
Related Theory
The presence of unpaired electrons leads to the formation of metal-metal covalent bonds along with the metallic bonds. These strong bonds attribute high melting and boiling points to the elements. The presence of a partially filled $d$-orbital enables the transition elements to have a greater number of unpaired electrons, which in turn increases their ability to form covalent bonds along with metallic bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The basic character of the transition metal monoxides follows the order:
(Atomic nos. $\mathrm{Ti}=22, \mathrm{~V}=23, \mathrm{Cr}=24, \mathrm{Fe}$ $=26$ )
questions.solution:
As we move from left side to right side in the first transition series atomic number of elements increases and no. of electrons also increases. Size of elements on moving left to right decreases because effective nuclear charge of nucleus on the outermost shell electron increases. It means electronegativity of atoms increases from left to right, then the power of donation of electrons decreases which means the basicity of that element decreases.
Caution
Students get confused on the order of size of elements in the series, because order of size of elements is not regular in the periods and groups. In periods of increasing atomic number size decreases and on the groups with the increase of atomic number size also increases.

questions.q: When $\mathrm{CuSO}_4$ reacts with $\mathrm{KCN}$ it forms $\mathrm{CuCN}$, which is insoluble in water. It is soluble in excess of $\mathrm{KCN}$ due to the formation of the following complex:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CuSO}_4$ reacts with $\mathrm{KCN}$ to give a white precipitate of cuprous cyanide and cyanogen gas. The cuprous cyanide dissolves in excess of $\mathrm{KCN}$ forming $\mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]$
$\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{CuSO}_4+2 \mathrm{KCN} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+ \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_2 \\
2 \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{CuCN}+\mathrm{CN}-\mathrm{CN} \\
\mathrm{CuCN}+3 \mathrm{KCN} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]
\end{gathered}$

questions.q: $\mathrm{Zn}$ gives $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas with $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$ but not with $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ because:
options: $\mathrm{Zn}$ acts as an oxidizing agent when reacts with $\mathrm{HNO}_3$
in electrochemical series $\mathrm{Zn}$ is above hydrogen
$\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$is reduced in preference to hydronium ion
questions.solution:
Nitric acid $\left(\mathrm{HNO}_3\right)$ is a strong oxidising agent. The Hydrogen gas produced during its reaction with metal gets oxidised to $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$, hence no hydrogen gas is produced.
Usually when $\mathrm{Zn}$ reacts with acid, it acts as a reducing agent which gets oxidised to a salt and the acid is the oxidising agent which gets reduced to hydrogen gas.

questions.solution: The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity. Reason (R): $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ oxidizes $\mathrm{I}^{-}$to $\mathrm{I}_2$
The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text{  } \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}}^{\circ}=+0.34 \mathrm{~V}, \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}^{-}}^{\circ}=0.54 \\ & 2 \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+4 \mathrm{I}^{-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{CuI}+\mathrm{I}_2\end{aligned}$
Despite the above values of the standard reduction potentials, $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ is able to oxidize iodide to $\mathrm{I}_2$ due to all the species like $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}, \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$, and $\mathrm{CuI}$ being present together in the solution.
The cumulative effect of this results in the $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \rightarrow \mathrm{CuI}$ reduction potential being $+0.88 \mathrm{~V}$ that makes the reaction feasible.
Therefore, $\mathrm{CuI} or \mathrm{Cu}_2 \mathrm{I}_2$ exists instead of $\mathrm{CuI}_2$ as $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ oxidises $\mathrm{I}^{-}$to $\mathrm{I}_2$ and so (A) and (R) are true with (R) explaining (A).

Transition elements are defined by the presence of partially filled \(d\) or \(f\) orbitals in any of their ions.

Step 5: Choose the appropriate answer based on the evaluations.
Given that Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct, the most appropriate answer is option (4): Statement-I is incorrect and II is correct.

I. The ionic radius of \($\mathrm{Pr}^{3+}, \mathrm{Dy}^{3+}$\) and \($\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$\) follow the order, \($\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}  \gt  \mathrm{Pr}^{3+}  \gt  \mathrm{Dy}^{3+}$\).
II. \($\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$\) acts as strong reducing reagent.
III. Pu exhibits +7 oxidation state.
questions.solution:
(i) The ionic radius of lanthanoids follow the following relation:
Ionic radius \(\propto \frac{1}{\text{ atomic number }}\)
Atomic number \((Z)\) for \(\mathrm{Pr}=59\)
Atomic number \((Z)\) for \(\mathrm{Sm}=62\)
Atomic number \((Z)\) for \(D y=66\)
and has ionic radii for positive ions as given below:
\begin{aligned}
$\mathrm{Pr}^{3+}$ & =1.013 Å \\
$\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$ & =0.964 Å \\
$\mathrm{Dy}^{3+}$ & =0.908 Å
\end{aligned}\)
Thus, statement (i) is not correct.
(ii) Element Eu \((Z=63)\) can exist in \((+) 2\) and \((+) 3\) oxidation state.
\(\therefore(+)\) 3oxidation state is the most common oxidation state for lanthanoids.
Thus, (+) 2oxidation state oxides oxidises to (+) 3 easily and \(\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}\) can act as strong reducing agent.
Hence, the statement (II) is correct.
(iii) The electronic configuation for
\(\text{(Pu), }(Z=94)=5 f^6 6 d^0 7 s^2\)
Therefore, it can use maximum of \(6+2=8\) electrons.
Thus, can show +7 oxidation state.
Thus, statement (III) is also correct.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
I. $\quad \mathrm{P}$ is having least negative electron gain enthalpy among $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{S}, \mathrm{Cl}$, and $\mathrm{F}$
II. In $\mathrm{Eu}, \mathrm{Yb}$ Lanthanoid contraction is not observed
III. $\mathrm{Ce}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is most basic among lanthanoid hydroxides
IV. The radii of $\mathrm{Na}$ and $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$are $95 \mathrm{pm}, 186 \mathrm{pm}$ respectively
questions.solution:
Europium $(\mathrm{Eu})=[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 \mathrm{f}^7 5 \mathrm{~d}^0 6 \mathrm{~s}^2, 185 \mathrm{pm}$ Ytterbium $(\mathrm{Yb})=[\mathrm{Xe}] 4 \mathrm{f}^{14} 5 \mathrm{~d}^0 6 \mathrm{~s}^2, 170 \mathrm{pm}$ In these two elements, the atomic radii do not show expected decrease due to lanthanoid contraction but instead show an increased value.
This is due to an electron entering into the $4 \mathrm{f}$-orbital(inner shell) and giving rise to very stable half-filled and fullyfilled configurations that results in greater screening of the valence electrons (higher screening constant $\sigma$ ) Thus, Statement II is correct.
The value of electron gain enthalpy is more negative for more electronegative elements.
The electronegativity follows the order :$\mathrm{P} < \mathrm{S} < \mathrm{Cl} < \mathrm{F}$.
Thus, $\mathrm{P}$ has the least negative electron gain enthalpy and therefore Statement I is correct.
$\mathrm{Ce}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is most basic hydroxide due to largest cation size which results in $\mathrm{Ce}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ being most ionic.
Thus, III is also correct.
The cation formed is always smaller than the parent atom or ion and thus $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$will be smaller than $\mathrm{Na}$.
Thus, IV is incorrect.

(i) $\mathrm{V}^{2+}$ liberates hydrogen from a dilute acid
(ii) The earlier members of lanthanide series behave more like aluminium
(iii) The 'silver' UK coins are made of $\mathrm{Cu} / \mathrm{Ni}$ alloy

questions.solution:

Silver $\mathrm{UK}$ coins $=\mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{Ni}$ alloy.
Thus, (iii) is correct.
Neptunium (Np) belongs to the actinides series and has the configuration $5 \mathrm{f}^4 6 \mathrm{~d}^{1 \cdot} 7 \mathrm{~s}^2$ because of which it can show a maximum of +7 oxidation state.
Thus, (iv) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(A) The ${M}^{3 +} / {M}^{2 +}$ reduction potential for iron is greater than manganese.

(B) The higher oxidation states of first row d-block elements get stabilized by oxide ion

(C) Aqueous solution of ${Cr}^{2 +}$ can liberate hydrogen from dilute acid

(D) Magnetic moment of ${V}^{2 +}$ is observed between $4 . 4 - 5 . 2BM$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The valence electronic configuration of ${Mn}^{3 +}$ is $3{d}^{4}$ and that of ${Mn}^{2 +}$ is stable $3{d}^{5}$.The valence electronic configuration of ${Fe}^{3 +}$ is $3{d}^{5}$ and that of ${Fe}^{2 +}$ is $3{d}^{6}$.

The reduction electrode potential of ${Mn}^{3 +} / {Mn}^{2 +}$ is $+ 1 . 57V$ while that of ${Fe}^{3 +} / {Fe}^{2 +}$ is $+ 0 . 77V$, hence A is wrong. Higher oxidation state of smaller $d$-block elements is stabilised (or say form compounds) with smaller anion oxide that can be explained by stearic reason hence $B$ is correct.

The oxidation electrode potential of ${Cr}^{2 +} / {Cr}^{3 +}$ is $+ 0 . 41V$ hence, it can reduce ${H}^{+}$ and so liberate ${H}_{2}$.

The unpaired electrons in ${V}^{2 +}$ are $3$ hence, the magnetic moment of ${V}^{2 +}$ will be lesser than $4 . 4BM$.

Hence, only $B$ and $C$ are correct.

Which one amongst the following are good oxidising agents?

(a) ${Sm}^{2 +}$

(b) ${Ce}^{2 +}$

(c) ${Ce}^{4 +}$

(d) ${Tb}^{4 +}$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The common oxidation state of lanthanide is $+ 3$. The lanthanide ions having $+ 2$ oxidation state undergo oxidation readily, hence they act as reducing agents. The lanthanide ions having  $+ 4$oxidation state undergo reduction readily, hence they act as oxidising agents.

Hence, ${Ce}^{+ 4}and{Tb}^{+ 4}$ act as oxidising agent

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The set of correct statements is:

(i) Manganese exhibits $+ 7$ oxidation state in its oxide.

(ii) Ruthenium and Osmium exhibit $+ 8$ oxidation in their oxides.

(iii) $Sc$ shows $+ 4$ oxidation state which is oxidizing in nature.

(iv) $Cr$ shows oxidising nature in $+ 6$ oxidation state.
questions.solution:
(i) The oxidation state of $Mn$ in oxide (${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$) is:

Let us consider $Mn$ as $x$.

$⇒ 2x + 7 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2x + ( - 14 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2x - 14 = 0$

$⇒ 2x = 14$

$⇒ x = 7$

(ii) The oxidation state of Ruthenium in oxide (${RuO}_{4}$) is:

Consider $Ru$ as $x$.

$⇒ x + 4 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = 8$

The oxidation state of Osmium in oxide (${OsO}_{4}$) is:

Consider $Os$ as $x$.

$⇒ x + 4 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = 8$ 

Hence, Ruthenium and Osmium has +7 oxidation state in its oxide.

(iii) $Sc$ has ${ns}^{2} ( n - 1 ) {d}^{1}$ electronic configuration.

It utilizes two electrons from its $ns$ sub-shell then its oxidation state = +2. When it utilizes both the electrons then its oxidation state = +3.

(iv) In the modern periodic table, chromium metal is present in group 6. It is a transition metal and belongs to the first transition series. The atomic number of chromium is 24. Its electronic configuration is $[ Ar ] 3{d}^{5}4{s}^{1}$. 

It has five electrons in the 3d sub-shell and one electron in the 4s sub-shell. Thus, chromium metal has six valence electrons. Chromium can lose some or all of its valence electrons to form ions with different oxidation states. Thus, chromium shows the oxidation states of +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, and +6 respectively.
The most common oxidation states of chromium are +2, +3, and +6.

So, the statement (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Highest oxidation state of $Mn$ is exhibited in ${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$. The correct statements about ${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$ are

(A) $Mn$ is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms
(B) $Mn$ is octahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms
(C) Contains $Mn - O - Mn$ bridge
(D) Contains $Mn - Mn$ bond.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.solution:
Each $Mn$ is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms. In addition, there is a bridging two-coordinated oxygen atom between two tetrahedral units. The bridged $Mn - O$ has different bond length than the tetrahedrally surrounded $Mn - O$ bond lengths.

 

So, the correct statement is only A and C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which one of the following statements are true?
$( 1 )$ Transition metals form alloys
$( 2 )$ Transition metals form complexes
$( 3 )$ Zn, Cd and Hg are transition metals
$( 4 )$ ${K}_{2}\left[PtC{l}_{6}\right]$ is a well known compound, but corresponding nickel compound is not known.
questions.solution:
Here statement (3) is not true as Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded transition metals, because the neutral atoms as well as stable ions have fully-filled d-orbitals.
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are true as transition metals have similar atomic sized, therefore, in the crystal lattice, one transition metals atoms can be easily replaced by the atoms of another transition metal to form alloy. They can easily form complexes, because they form small highly charged cations, which have vacant orbitals of suitable energy to accept electron pairs donated by ligands.
As the sum of first four ionization energies of Pt is less than the sum of first four ionization energies of Ni, so ${K}_{2}\left[PtC{l}_{6}\right]$ is more stable than the corresponding nickel compound.

Pick out the correct statement set for transition metals
$1 .$ They form interstitial compounds
$2 .$ 5d-elements have higher energies than 3d or 4d-elements
$3 .$ Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic and ionic radii
$4 .$ They have low melting and boiling points (or low enthalpies of atomization)
questions.solution:
Here statement 1, 2 and 3 are correct as follows

Because small size, atoms of H, C, N occupy the vacant spaces in the crystal lattice of transition metal.

This due to the greater effective nuclear charge acting on outer valence electrons, because of weak shielding of nucleus by 4f-electrons

The normal size increase from Zr to Hf is almost exactly balanced by lanthanide contraction

Transition metals have high enthalpies of atomization, because they form strong metallic bonds, due to participation of (n – 1) d-electrons along with ns-electrons in metallic bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the set having incorrect statements given here.
(i) Manganese exhibits +7 oxidation state
(ii) Zinc forms coloured ions
(iii) $[ \text{Co}{\text{F}}_{6}{]}^{3 -}$ is diamagnetic
(iv) Sc forms +4 oxidation state
(v) Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state
questions.solution:
Outer electronic configuration of Mn is $\text{3}{\text{d}}^{5}\text{4}{\text{s}}^{2}$ which means it can show +7 oxidation state also (correct)
Zinc does not form coloured ions as it has completely filled $\text{3}{\text{d}}^{10}\text{4}{\text{s}}^{2}$ configuration.
In $[ \text{Co}{\text{F}}_{6}{]}^{3 -}, \text{C}{\text{o}}^{3 +}$ is a ${d}^{6}$ system. Fluoride is a weak field ligand and hence it can not cause pairing of electrons.

Sc can show a maximum of +3 oxidation state as it has an outer electronic configuration of $\text{3}{\text{d}}^{1}\text{4}{\text{s}}^{2}$ .
Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state as this oxidation state is the most stable one for it.
Hence (ii), (iii), (iv) are incorrect while (i), (v) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify all the correct statements for Lanthanide contraction.
(A) The covalent properties of the Lanthanide metal hydroxides increases from $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$.
(B) The chemical reactivity decreases from $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$.
(C) $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$
(D) Zr and Hf have about the same radius.
(E) Separation of Lanthanides from one another is easy
questions.solution:
The change in ionic radii is Lanthanide series is very small, their chemical properties are small. Thus, the separation of Lanthanide is difficult due to consequence of Lanthanide contraction.
The ionic radii of same positive charge of $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$ decreases. So, the polarizing power towards hydroxyl group increases. Therefore the covalent character increases. Thus, $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$. $\mathrm{Zr}$ and $\mathrm{Hf}$ have the almost same radius as the electrons in the elements after $\mathrm{Zr}$ are added into the deep seated $4 \mathrm{f}$ orbitals which do not take part in the chemical reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statement is correct.
(A) In Lanthanide series metallic radius regularly decreases from La to Lu .
(B) La is actually an elements of transition series rather than lanthanide.
(C) \(\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3\) is less basic than \(\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3\)
(D) The atomic radius of Zr & Hf are nearly similar because of lanthanoid contraction.
options: If A, B and C options are correct.
If A & B both options are correct.
If A & D both are options correct.
If A & C both are options correct.
questions.solution:
(A) Correct. In the Lanthanide series, the metallic radius decreases from La to Lu due to the lanthanide contraction, which is caused by the poor shielding of the nuclear charge by the \(4 f\) electrons.
(B) Incorrect. Lanthanum (La) is considered a member of the Lanthanide series, not the transition series.
(C) Incorrect. \(\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3\) is more basic than \(\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3\) because the basicity increases with the decrease in size of the metal ion.
(D) Correct. The atomic radii of Zr and Hf are nearly similar due to the lanthanide contraction, which affects the size of the atoms in the 6th period.

questions.q:
Match the column : \(
Column IColumn II
(Property)(Element)
(i)$\begin{array}{l} Lanthanoid which show
+4 oxidation state \end{array}$(a)Pm
(ii)$\begin{array}{l} Lanthanoid which can show
+2 oxidation state \end{array}$(b)Gd
(iii)Radioactive lanthanoid(c)Ce
(iv)$\begin{array}{l} Lanthanoid which has
4 f^7 configuration in
+3 oxidation state \end{array}$(d)Eu
\)
questions.solution:
(i) Lanthanoid which shows +4 oxidation state:
Answer: (c) Ce
Cerium (Ce) is the only lanthanoid that can exhibit a +4 oxidation state. This is due to its relatively low ionization energy for the fourth electron.
(ii) Lanthanoid which can show +2 oxidation state:
Answer: (d) Eu
Europium (Eu) can exhibit a +2 oxidation state. This is because the half-filled \(4 f^{7}\) configuration provides extra stability.
(iii) Radioactive lanthanoid:
Answer: (a) Pm
Promethium (Pm) is the only radioactive lanthanoid found in nature. All other lanthanoids are relatively stable.
(iv) Lanthanoid which has \(4f7\) configuration in \(+3\) oxidation state:
Answer: (b) Gd
Gadolinium (Gd) has a \(4 f^{7}\) configuration in its \(+3\) oxidation state. This half-filled configuration provides extra stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding d-block elements:
(I) Chromium has the maximum number of unpaired electrons in its ground state among the $3\text{d}$ series elements.
(II) The highest oxidation state shown by any transition element is $+8$, which is exhibited by Osmium.
(III) Copper is the only metal in the $3\text{d}$ series with a positive standard reduction potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$).
(IV) Zinc, Cadmium, and Mercury are hard metals with high melting points due to strong metallic bonding.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct: Chromium has the electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^{5} 4\text{s}^{1}$, giving it $6$ unpaired electrons, which is the maximum in the $3\text{d}$ series.

Statement (II) is correct: Osmium (and Ruthenium) can exhibit an oxidation state of $+8$, the highest among transition elements.

Statement (III) is correct: Copper has a positive standard reduction potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = +0.34\text{ V}$), while all other $3\text{d}$ series metals have negative values.

Statement (IV) is incorrect: Zinc, Cadmium, and Mercury have completely filled d-orbitals which do not participate in metallic bonding. Consequently, they have weak metallic bonds, making them soft metals with low melting points.

Therefore, exactly $3$ statements are correct.

Answer: $3$

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the f-block elements is incorrect?
options: Actinoid contraction from element to element is greater than lanthanoid contraction due to poorer shielding by $5f$ electrons.
Actinoids exhibit a larger number of oxidation states because of the very small energy gap between $5f$, $6d$ and $7s$ subshells.

The first ionization enthalpies of early actinoids are higher than those of the corresponding early lanthanoids.
questions.solution:
The first ionization enthalpies of early actinoids are actually lower than those of the early lanthanoids. This is because $5f$ electrons penetrate less into the inner core and are less tightly bound by the nucleus compared to $4f$ electrons, making them easier to remove.

The other statements are correct facts regarding f-block elements. Actinoid contraction is greater due to the poorer shielding effect of $5f$ electrons compared to $4f$ electrons. The small energy gap between $5f$, $6d$, and $7s$ allows actinoids to show a wide variety of oxidation states, though $+3$ remains the most common for both series.

Answer: The first ionization enthalpies of early actinoids are higher than those of the corresponding early lanthanoids.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The oxidation of ethyne to ethanal is catalysed by a compound of a 3d-series transition element.
Reason (R): Palladium chloride ($\mathrm{PdCl}_2$) catalyses the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal, and palladium belongs to the 4d-series of transition elements.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal is catalysed by $\mathrm{PdCl}_2$ (Wacker process), and palladium (Pd) is a 4d-series transition element (Group 10), not a 3d-series element. A student might incorrectly assume it is a 3d element if they confuse it with nickel complexes which are used for alkyne polymerisation.

Reason (R) is true because palladium chloride ($\mathrm{PdCl}_2$) is indeed the catalyst for this reaction, and palladium is located in the 4d series of the periodic table.

Therefore, Assertion is false but Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following oxides of manganese: $\mathrm{MnO}, \mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_3, \mathrm{MnO}_2$, and $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$.

Identify the acid-base nature of the oxide with the highest oxidation state of manganese, and calculate the spin-only magnetic moment (in BM) of the manganese ion in the most basic oxide among these.
questions.solution:
The oxidation states of manganese in the given oxides are: $\mathrm{MnO}$ (+2), $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ (+3), $\mathrm{MnO}_2$ (+4), and $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ (+7).

As the oxidation state of a transition metal increases, the acidic character of its oxide increases. Therefore, the oxide with the highest oxidation state, $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$, is acidic in nature.

The most basic oxide is the one with the lowest oxidation state, which is $\mathrm{MnO}$ (+2).

In $\mathrm{MnO}$, the manganese ion is $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$. The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^5$.
The number of unpaired electrons ($n$) is 5.
The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is calculated as:
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92 \text{ BM}$.

Thus, the highest oxidation state oxide is acidic, and the magnetic moment of the metal in the most basic oxide is $5.92 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: Acidic, $5.92 \text{ BM}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of elements exhibits almost identical atomic radii as a direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction?
questions.solution:
Due to lanthanoid contraction, the atomic radii of the elements of the 5d transition series are very similar to those of the corresponding elements of the 4d series. This effect is observed from Group 4 onwards because the filling of 4f orbitals occurs after Lanthanum ($\text{La}$, $Z=57$). Therefore, Niobium ($\text{Nb}$, 4d series) and Tantalum ($\text{Ta}$, 5d series) have almost identical atomic radii.

The pair $\text{Y}$ and $\text{La}$ (Group 3) does not show this effect as $\text{La}$ precedes the 4f series. $\text{Ti}$ and $\text{Zr}$ are 3d and 4d elements respectively, and their radii differ significantly as expected down a group. $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Mg}$ belong to the s-block and their similarity in size is due to a diagonal relationship, not lanthanoid contraction.

Answer: $\text{Nb}$ and $\text{Ta}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Terbium (IV) acts as an oxidant in aqueous solution.

Reason (R): The $+4$ oxidation state of Terbium is favoured by its noble gas core electronic configuration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Terbium (Tb) can show a $+4$ oxidation state, but the most stable oxidation state for all lanthanoids is $+3$. Thus, $Tb^{4+}$ readily accepts an electron to become $Tb^{3+}$, acting as a strong oxidant in aqueous solutions.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The atomic number of Terbium is $65$. The electronic configuration of Tb is $[Xe] 4f^{9} 6s^{2}$. In the $+4$ oxidation state, the configuration of $Tb^{4+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{7}$. This represents a stable half-filled $f$-subshell, not a noble gas core configuration (which would be $4f^{0}$, as seen in $Ce^{4+}$).

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the electronic configuration and redox behaviour of lanthanoid ions is incorrect?
options: $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ has a $4f^{7}$ configuration and acts as a strong reducing agent.
$\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ has a half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration and acts as a strong reducing agent.
$\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$ has a fully-filled $4f^{14}$ configuration and acts as a reducing agent.
$\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ has a noble gas configuration but acts as a strong oxidising agent.
questions.solution:
The most stable oxidation state for lanthanoids is $+3$. Ions in the $+2$ state tend to lose an electron to reach $+3$, acting as reducing agents, while ions in the $+4$ state tend to gain an electron to reach $+3$, acting as oxidising agents.

$\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ ($4f^{7}$) and $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$ ($4f^{14}$) are in the $+2$ oxidation state and act as reducing agents to reach the $+3$ state.

$\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ (noble gas configuration) and $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ ($4f^{7}$) are in the $+4$ oxidation state. Despite the stability of their respective electronic configurations, both act as strong oxidising agents by gaining an electron to revert to the common $+3$ state.

Therefore, the statement claiming $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ acts as a reducing agent is incorrect.

Answer: $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ has a half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration and acts as a strong reducing agent.

$\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ ($4f^{7}$) and $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$ ($4f^{14}$) are in the $+2$ oxidation state and act as reducing agents to reach the $+3$ state.

$\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ (noble gas configuration) and $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ ($4f^{7}$) are in the $+4$ oxidation state. Despite the stability of their respective electronic configurations, both act as strong oxidising agents by gaining an electron to revert to the common $+3$ state.

Therefore, the statement claiming $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ acts as a reducing agent is incorrect.

Answer: $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ has a half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration and acts as a strong reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The atomic radius of Niobium ($\text{Nb}$) is almost the same as that of Tantalum ($\text{Ta}$).

Reason (R): The poor shielding effect of 4f electrons in Tantalum leads to an increase in effective nuclear charge, which cancels out the expected increase in size down the group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Niobium ($\text{Nb}$) belongs to the 4d transition series, while Tantalum ($\text{Ta}$) belongs to the 5d transition series, both residing in Group 5. Normally, atomic radius increases down a group due to the addition of a new principal quantum shell.

However, before the filling of 5d orbitals in Tantalum, the 4f orbitals are filled (lanthanoid contraction). The 4f electrons provide very poor shielding for the outer electrons from the increasing nuclear charge. This results in a higher effective nuclear charge that pulls the valence electrons closer, causing a contraction in size. This contraction almost perfectly cancels out the expected increase in size from the 4d to the 5d series. Therefore, $\text{Nb}$ and $\text{Ta}$ have almost identical atomic radii.

Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The characteristic narrow absorption bands in the spectra of lanthanoid ions arise due to $f-f$ transitions. Which of the following lanthanoid ions will NOT exhibit these absorption bands?
questions.solution:
The narrow absorption bands in lanthanoids are due to the excitation of electrons within the $4f$ subshell ($f-f$ transitions). For these transitions to occur, the ion must have a partially filled $4f$ subshell ($4f^{1}$ to $4f^{13}$).

The electronic configurations of the given ions are:
$\text{Eu}^{3+}$ ($Z = 63$): $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{6}$
$\text{Pr}^{3+}$ ($Z = 59$): $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{2}$
$\text{Sm}^{3+}$ ($Z = 62$): $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{5}$
$\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($Z = 71$): $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14}$

Since $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ has a fully filled $4f$ subshell, it cannot undergo $f-f$ transitions and therefore does not exhibit these characteristic absorption bands.

Answer: $\text{Lu}^{3+}$

questions.q: In the first transition series, the melting points of the metals generally increase with atomic number, reach a maximum, and then decrease regularly. However, one specific metal situated near the middle of the series exhibits an anomalous dip in its melting point. What is the ground state outer electronic configuration of the metal showing this anomalous dip?
questions.solution:
In the first transition series ($3d$ series), the melting point generally increases as the number of unpaired $d$-electrons increases, reaching a maximum at chromium (Cr, $3d^{5} 4s^{1}$).

However, manganese (Mn) and technetium (Tc) in the $4d$ series show an anomalous dip in their melting points despite having a $d^{5}$ configuration.

The metal in the first transition series that exhibits this anomalous dip is manganese (Mn).

The ground state outer electronic configuration of manganese is $3d^{5} 4s^{2}$.

Answer: $3d^{5} 4s^{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the ratio of the number of moles of $KMnO_4$ required to completely oxidise one mole of $KI$ in an acidic medium to that in a faintly alkaline medium?
questions.solution:
In an acidic medium, $KMnO_4$ oxidises iodide ($I^-$) to iodine ($I_2$) and itself gets reduced to $Mn^{2+}$.
The n-factor for $KI$ is $1$ (since $2I^- \rightarrow I_2 + 2e^-$, so $1$ mole of $I^-$ loses $1$ mole of $e^-$).
The n-factor for $KMnO_4$ is $5$ ($Mn^{+7} \rightarrow Mn^{+2}$).
Equating the number of equivalents:
Moles of $KMnO_4 \times 5 = \text{Moles of } KI \times 1$
$n_1 \times 5 = 1 \times 1 \Rightarrow n_1 = \dfrac{1}{5}$ moles.

In a faintly alkaline medium, $KMnO_4$ oxidises iodide ($I^-$) to iodate ($IO_3^-$) and itself gets reduced to $MnO_2$.
The n-factor for $KI$ is $6$ ($I^- \rightarrow IO_3^-$, change in oxidation state from $-1$ to $+5$).
The n-factor for $KMnO_4$ is $3$ ($Mn^{+7} \rightarrow Mn^{+4}$).
Equating the number of equivalents:
Moles of $KMnO_4 \times 3 = \text{Moles of } KI \times 6$
$n_2 \times 3 = 1 \times 6 \Rightarrow n_2 = 2$ moles.

The required ratio is $n_1 : n_2 = \dfrac{1}{5} : 2 = 1 : 10$.

Answer: $1:10$

questions.q: Among the lanthanoids, Europium readily forms stable $Eu^{2+}$ ions in solid compounds and in solution. Which of the following best explains the stability of this specific oxidation state?
options: The $Eu^{2+}$ ion attains a fully-filled $4f^{14}$ subshell.
The removal of two electrons leaves behind a noble gas core.
The resulting ion possesses a $4f^{6} 5d^{1}$ configuration.
The formation of the ion results in an exactly half-filled $4f^{7}$ subshell.
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Europium (Eu) is $63$.

The ground state electronic configuration of Eu is $[Xe] 4f^{7} 6s^{2}$.

When it loses two electrons to form the $Eu^{2+}$ ion, the electrons are removed from the outermost $6s$ orbital.

The electronic configuration of $Eu^{2+}$ becomes $[Xe] 4f^{7}$.

This configuration features a half-filled $f$-subshell, which imparts extra stability to the $+2$ oxidation state.

Thus, the stability of $Eu^{2+}$ is due to the acquisition of a half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration.

Answer: The formation of the ion results in an exactly half-filled $4f^{7}$ subshell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Transition metals act as effective catalysts because of their ability to change their oxidation states. In the Contact process, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ catalyses the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$. During this catalytic cycle, the $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is initially reduced to an intermediate compound before being re-oxidised by atmospheric oxygen.

What is the oxidation state of vanadium in this intermediate compound?
questions.solution:
The catalytic action of $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ in the Contact process involves a change in the oxidation state of vanadium. The reaction proceeds via the following mechanism:

$\text{SO}_2 + \text{V}_2\text{O}_5 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 + \text{V}_2\text{O}_4$

$\text{V}_2\text{O}_4 + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{V}_2\text{O}_5$

In the intermediate compound $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$, the oxidation state of vanadium is +4. It is then re-oxidised by oxygen back to the +5 state in $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$.

Answer: +4

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(I) Transition metals act as catalysts due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and form complexes.
(II) $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ catalyses the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ in the Contact process.
(III) Finely divided iron is used as a catalyst in the Ostwald process for the manufacture of nitric acid.
(IV) Ziegler-Natta catalyst involves a titanium compound and is used for the polymerisation of ethene.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct as the catalytic activity of transition metals is attributed to their ability to show variable oxidation states and form complexes.

Statement (II) is correct as $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is the catalyst used in the Contact process for the manufacture of sulphuric acid.

Statement (III) is incorrect because finely divided iron is used in the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia. The Ostwald process for nitric acid uses a platinised asbestos or Pt/Rh gauge catalyst.

Statement (IV) is correct as the Ziegler-Natta catalyst contains $\text{TiCl}_4$ (a titanium compound) and is used for the polymerisation of ethene.

Therefore, exactly 3 statements are correct.

Answer: 3

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution:
Statement I is correct because the actinoid contraction is greater from element to element compared to the lanthanoid contraction.

Statement II is incorrect because the $5f$ electrons have a poorer shielding effect than the $4f$ electrons. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The standard electrode potentials $\left(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\right)$ for the $\mathrm{M}^{2+} / \mathrm{M}$ couple of some $3d$ series elements are observed as follows: $\mathrm{V} (-1.18 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Cr} (-0.90 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Mn} (-1.18 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Fe} (-0.44 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Ni} (-0.25 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Cu} (+0.34 \mathrm{V})$, and $\mathrm{Zn} (-0.76 \mathrm{V})$.

While the general trend across the series is that the $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value becomes less negative, $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ break this trend by exhibiting more negative values than expected. Which of the following statements correctly explains this anomaly?
options: $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ have exceptionally high enthalpies of atomisation compared to other transition metals.
The hydration enthalpies of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ are exceptionally high, making their formation highly favourable.

The formation of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ is thermodynamically favoured due to their stable exactly half-filled $\left(d^5\right)$ and fully-filled $\left(d^{10}\right)$ configurations respectively.
$\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ achieve stability by attaining $d^4$ and $d^9$ electronic configurations respectively.
questions.solution:
The standard electrode potential $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{M}^{2+} / \mathrm{M}\right)$ depends on the sum of the enthalpy of atomisation, ionisation enthalpies ($\Delta_i \mathrm{H}_1 + \Delta_i \mathrm{H}_2$), and hydration enthalpy.

Across the $3d$ series, the general trend is a less negative $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value due to the general increase in the sum of the first and second ionisation enthalpies.

However, $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ have more negative $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ values than the trend predicts. This is because the $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ion has a stable exactly half-filled $3d^5$ configuration, and the $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ ion has a stable fully-filled $3d^{10}$ configuration.

The extra thermodynamic stability of these configurations lowers the required ionisation energy to form the $+2$ state, making the overall $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value more negative. The other options are incorrect: $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ actually have low enthalpies of atomisation, and their configurations are $d^5$ and $d^{10}$, not $d^4$ and $d^9$.

Answer: The formation of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ is thermodynamically favoured due to their stable exactly half-filled $\left(d^5\right)$ and fully-filled $\left(d^{10}\right)$ configurations respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The absorption bands in the electronic spectra of actinoid ions are relatively broader and more complex compared to the narrow bands of lanthanoid ions. What is the primary reason for this difference?
options: The $5f$ orbitals are less deeply buried than the $4f$ orbitals, allowing stronger interaction with surrounding ligands.
The $5f$ orbitals are more deeply buried than the $4f$ orbitals, resulting in complete shielding from the ligand field.
The absorption in actinoid ions is primarily due to $d-d$ transitions rather than $f-f$ transitions.
Actinoids possess significantly higher first ionization enthalpies than lanthanoids.
questions.solution:
In lanthanoids, the $4f$ orbitals are deeply buried and well-shielded by the outer $5s$ and $5p$ electrons, leading to narrow, line-like absorption bands because the ligand field has very little effect on them.

In contrast, the $5f$ orbitals in actinoids are less deeply buried and extend further outward than the $4f$ orbitals. As a result, they are less effectively shielded and interact more strongly with the surrounding ligand environment. This stronger ligand field interaction leads to broader and more complex absorption bands in actinoids.

Assertion (A): $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ is an acidic oxide whereas $\mathrm{MnO}$ is a basic oxide.
Reason (R): In transition metal oxides, as the oxidation state of the metal increases, the ionic character of the metal-oxygen bond increases, which makes the oxide more acidic.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: The oxidation state of manganese in $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ is +7, making it an acidic oxide. In $\mathrm{MnO}$, the oxidation state is +2, making it a basic oxide.

Reason (R) is false: According to Fajans' rules, as the positive charge (oxidation state) on the metal ion increases, its polarizing power increases. This leads to an increase in the covalent character of the metal-oxygen bond, not the ionic character. The higher covalent character facilitates the release of $\mathrm{H}^+$ ions in aqueous medium, thereby increasing the acidic nature of the oxide.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sets of lanthanoid ions acts as good reducing agents in aqueous solutions?
questions.solution:
The most stable oxidation state for all lanthanoids is +3.

Ions in the +2 oxidation state (such as $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$) tend to lose one electron to achieve the more stable +3 state. Since they undergo oxidation, they act as good reducing agents.

Conversely, ions in the +4 state (like $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ and $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$) tend to gain an electron to reach the +3 state, acting as oxidising agents.

Answer: $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$

questions.q: The $+3$ oxidation state is the most characteristic state for lanthanoids. Considering this, what is the expected chemical behavior of $Ce^{4+}$ and $Eu^{2+}$ ions when present in an aqueous solution?
options: $Ce^{4+}$ acts as a strong oxidizing agent, while $Eu^{2+}$ acts as a strong reducing agent.
$Ce^{4+}$ acts as a strong reducing agent, while $Eu^{2+}$ acts as a strong oxidizing agent.
Both $Ce^{4+}$ and $Eu^{2+}$ act as strong oxidizing agents to achieve the $+3$ state.
Both ions are chemically inert in aqueous solution due to their stable $f^{0}$ and $f^{7}$ configurations respectively.
questions.solution:
The most stable and characteristic oxidation state for all lanthanoids in aqueous solution is $+3$.

Cerium in the $+4$ state has a stable $4f^{0}$ configuration, but it strongly tends to revert to the more thermodynamically stable $+3$ state. By gaining an electron ($Ce^{4+} + e^{-} \rightarrow Ce^{3+}$), it acts as a strong oxidizing agent.

Europium in the $+2$ state has a stable half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration. However, it also tends to achieve the common $+3$ state by losing an electron ($Eu^{2+} \rightarrow Eu^{3+} + e^{-}$). Thus, it acts as a strong reducing agent.

Therefore, $Ce^{4+}$ is an oxidizing agent and $Eu^{2+}$ is a reducing agent.

Answer: $Ce^{4+}$ acts as a strong oxidizing agent, while $Eu^{2+}$ acts as a strong reducing agent.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ ion (Z = 63) is strongly paramagnetic with a spin-only magnetic moment of approximately 7.9 BM.

Reason (R): The $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ ion is formed by the loss of two electrons from the $4\mathrm{f}$ subshell of the Europium atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of the Europium atom (Z = 63) is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^7 6\mathrm{s}^2$.

The $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ ion is formed by the loss of two electrons from the outermost $6\mathrm{s}$ subshell, not the $4\mathrm{f}$ subshell. Therefore, Reason (R) is false.

The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^7$. It has 7 unpaired electrons.

The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is calculated as:
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$
$\mu = \sqrt{7(7+2)} = \sqrt{63} \approx 7.9 \text{ BM}$

Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of catalysts is used for the polymerisation of ethylene and the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal, respectively?
questions.solution:
The polymerisation of ethylene to manufacture polyethylene is catalysed by the Ziegler-Natta catalyst, which is a mixture of titanium tetrachloride ($\mathrm{TiCl_4}$) and trimethylaluminium ($\mathrm{Al(CH_3)_3}$).

The oxidation of ethyne to ethanal is catalysed by palladium(II) chloride ($\mathrm{PdCl_2}$).

Therefore, the correct respective pair of catalysts is $\mathrm{TiCl_4} + \mathrm{Al(CH_3)_3}$ and $\mathrm{PdCl_2}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{TiCl_4} + \mathrm{Al(CH_3)_3}$ and $\mathrm{PdCl_2}$

questions.q: An amphoteric oxide of a 3d transition metal 'M' dissolves in acids to give a salt containing the oxocation $\text{MO}^{2+}$. The spin-only magnetic moment of the metal ion in this oxide is:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the amphoteric oxide of a 3d transition metal that dissolves in acids to give the $\text{MO}^{2+}$ oxocation is $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$ (which gives $\text{VO}^{2+}$ salts).

In $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$, the oxidation state of vanadium is $+4$.
The electronic configuration of neutral V atom (Z = 23) is $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^3 4\text{s}^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{V}^{4+}$ ion is $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^1$.

Since there is $1$ unpaired electron ($n = 1$), the spin-only magnetic moment is:
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} = 1.73 \text{ BM}$.

Students who confuse this with $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ (which gives $\text{VO}_2^+$ in acids) would incorrectly calculate $0 \text{ BM}$ for $\text{V}^{5+}$.

Answer: $1.73 \text{ BM}$

options: $Mn_2O_7$ is an acidic oxide and is a covalent green oil at room temperature.

Answer: $CrO_3$ is a basic oxide that dissolves in dilute acids to give $Cr^{3+}$ ions.

Assertion (A): The standard reduction potential $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{M}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}^{2+}}$ for manganese is much more positive than that for iron.

Reason (R): $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ ($d^4$) is easily reduced to the highly stable $d^5$ configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$, whereas $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ already possesses a stable $d^5$ configuration and resists reduction to $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$).

options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the melting points and metallic bonding of $d$-block elements:
(A) The high melting points of transition metals are attributed to the involvement of only $(n-1)d$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
(B) In any transition series, the melting point generally rises to a maximum at $d^{5}$ configuration.
(C) Zinc, cadmium and mercury are hard metals with high melting points.
(D) The strength of the metallic bond decreases as the number of unpaired $d$-electrons increases.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect. According to NCERT, the high melting points of transition metals are attributed to the involvement of a greater number of electrons from the $(n-1)d$ subshell in addition to the $ns$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.

Statement (B) is correct. In any transition series, the melting point generally rises to a maximum at $d^{5}$ configuration (except for anomalous values of $\text{Mn}$ and $\text{Tc}$) and then falls regularly as the atomic number increases.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Zinc, cadmium and mercury have fully filled $d$-subshells ($d^{10}$) and their $d$-electrons do not participate in metallic bonding. Hence, they are soft metals with exceptionally low melting points.

Statement (D) is incorrect. The strength of the metallic bond increases as the number of unpaired $d$-electrons increases, which leads to higher enthalpies of atomisation and melting points.

Therefore, only one statement (B) is correct.

Answer: Only one

Statement (C) is incorrect. Zinc, cadmium and mercury have fully filled $d$-subshells ($d^{10}$) and their $d$-electrons do not participate in metallic bonding. Hence, they are soft metals with exceptionally low melting points.

Statement (D) is incorrect. The strength of the metallic bond increases as the number of unpaired $d$-electrons increases, which leads to higher enthalpies of atomisation and melting points.

Therefore, only one statement (B) is correct.

Answer: Only one

questions.q: Identify the INCORRECT pairing of a $3\text{d}$ series metal's unique property and the magnetic characteristic of its specified ion.
options: Zinc: Not considered a transition metal; its $+2$ ion is diamagnetic.
Scandium: Does not show variable oxidation states; its $+3$ ion is diamagnetic.
Copper: Its $+1$ ion undergoes disproportionation in aqueous solution; its $+2$ ion is paramagnetic.
Manganese: Shows the maximum number of oxidation states in the $3\text{d}$ series; its $+2$ ion has $4$ unpaired electrons.
questions.solution:
Option 1 is a correct pairing: Zinc ($3\text{d}^{10} 4\text{s}^{2}$) is not considered a transition metal because it has completely filled d-orbitals in its ground state and its common $+2$ oxidation state. The $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ion ($3\text{d}^{10}$) has no unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

Option 2 is a correct pairing: Scandium only shows a $+3$ oxidation state and does not exhibit variable oxidation states. The $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ion ($3\text{d}^{0}$) is diamagnetic.

Option 3 is a correct pairing: Copper(I) undergoes disproportionation in aqueous solution ($2\text{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Cu}$). The $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion ($3\text{d}^{9}$) has one unpaired electron and is paramagnetic.

Option 4 is the incorrect pairing: While Manganese does show the maximum number of oxidation states (up to $+7$) in the $3\text{d}$ series, its $+2$ ion ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$) has the electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^{5}$. Therefore, it has $5$ unpaired electrons, not $4$.

Answer: Manganese: Shows the maximum number of oxidation states in the $3\text{d}$ series; its $+2$ ion has $4$ unpaired electrons.

questions.q: Despite having the same $d^4$ electronic configuration, $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ acts as a strong reducing agent while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ acts as a strong oxidising agent. What is the correct reason for this contrasting behaviour?
options: $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ which has a stable $d^5$ configuration, while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ which has a stable $d^3$ configuration.
$\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ acts as an oxidising agent to achieve a stable $d^0$ configuration, while $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ acts as a reducing agent to achieve a stable $d^0$ configuration.

$\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Cr}^{+}$ which has a stable half-filled $d$-subshell, while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{Mn}^{4+}$ which has a stable half-filled $t_{2g}$ level.

$\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ which has a stable half-filled $t_{2g}$ level ($d^3$), while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ which has a stable half-filled $d$-subshell ($d^5$).
questions.solution:
A reducing agent gets oxidised, meaning it loses an electron. $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ ($d^4$) loses one electron to form $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ ($d^3$). In an aqueous medium, the $d^3$ configuration is exceptionally stable due to an exactly half-filled $t_{2g}$ level.

An oxidising agent gets reduced, meaning it gains an electron. $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ ($d^4$) gains one electron to form $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ($d^5$). The $d^5$ configuration is highly stable due to an exactly half-filled $d$-subshell.

Therefore, the contrasting behaviour is driven by the stability of the final configurations achieved: $d^3$ for $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ and $d^5$ for $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ which has a stable half-filled $t_{2g}$ level ($d^3$), while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ which has a stable half-filled $d$-subshell ($d^5$).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The acid-base nature of transition metal oxides depends on the oxidation state of the metal. As the oxidation state increases, the acidic character increases.

$\mathrm{MnO}$ has Mn in the +2 oxidation state, which is a low oxidation state, making it basic. Thus, (A) matches with (III).

$\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ has Cr in the +3 oxidation state, which is an intermediate state, making it amphoteric. Thus, (B) matches with (I).

$\mathrm{CrO}_3$ has Cr in the +6 oxidation state, making it acidic. It dissolves in water to give chromic acid ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CrO}_4$) and dichromic acid ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7$). Thus, (C) matches with (IV).

$\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ has Mn in the +7 oxidation state, making it strongly acidic. It dissolves in water to give permanganic acid ($\mathrm{HMnO}_4$). Thus, (D) matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following transition metal ions has a calculated spin-only magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ BM}$?
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.92 \text{ BM}$, we can find $n$ by approximating $\sqrt{n(n+2)} \approx 5.92$. Since $\sqrt{35} \approx 5.916$, we have $n(n+2) = 35$, which gives $n = 5$ unpaired electrons.

Now, let us evaluate the number of unpaired electrons for each given ion:

$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ (Atomic number $26$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 \Rightarrow 4$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Mn}^{2+}$ (Atomic number $25$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 \Rightarrow 5$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Cr}^{3+}$ (Atomic number $24$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^3 \Rightarrow 3$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Mn}^{3+}$ (Atomic number $25$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4 \Rightarrow 4$ unpaired electrons.

Thus, $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ has $5$ unpaired electrons and corresponds to a magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $\text{Mn}^{2+}$

questions.q: Among the elements of the first transition series, zinc exhibits the lowest enthalpy of atomisation ($126 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). What is the primary fundamental reason for this observation?
options: The high effective nuclear charge of zinc tightly binds its valence electrons.
The exceptional stability of its completely filled $4s$ orbital prevents metallic bonding.
The absence of unpaired electrons in its $3d$ subshell leads to weak interatomic metallic bonding.
The relatively larger atomic radius of zinc decreases the electrostatic attraction between atoms.
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of atomisation is a direct measure of the strength of interatomic metallic bonds in a solid lattice.

In transition metals, the strength of metallic bonding depends largely on the number of unpaired electrons available in the $(n-1)d$ subshell, which participate in bonding along with the $ns$ electrons.

Zinc has a ground state electronic configuration of $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^{2}$. Because its $3d$ subshell is completely filled, it possesses no unpaired $d$-electrons to contribute to the metallic bond.

This lack of unpaired $d$-electrons results in very weak interatomic metallic bonding, which is why zinc has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation in the $3d$ series.

Answer: The absence of unpaired electrons in its $3d$ subshell leads to weak interatomic metallic bonding.

Consider the following statements regarding the chromate and dichromate ions:
(I) The yellow colour of chromate ion changes to orange dichromate ion in acidic medium.
(II) During the conversion of chromate to dichromate, the oxidation state of chromium changes from $+6$ to $+7$.
(III) The chromate ion has a tetrahedral geometry.
(IV) The dichromate ion consists of two tetrahedra sharing one oxygen corner with a $\text{Cr}-\text{O}-\text{Cr}$ bond angle of $126^{\circ}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct: Chromate ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$) is yellow and changes to orange dichromate ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$) in acidic medium.

Statement (II) is incorrect: The oxidation state of chromium in both chromate and dichromate ions is $+6$. The interconversion is a pH-dependent equilibrium, not a redox reaction.

Statement (III) is correct: The chromate ion has a tetrahedral geometry.

Statement (IV) is correct: The dichromate ion consists of two tetrahedra sharing one oxygen corner with a $\text{Cr}-\text{O}-\text{Cr}$ bond angle of $126^{\circ}$.

Therefore, exactly 3 statements are correct.

Answer: 3

Consider the following statements regarding the catalytic applications of $d$-block elements and their compounds:
(a) $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ catalyses the oxidation of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ in the manufacture of sulphuric acid.
(b) $\mathrm{TiCl_4}$ with $\mathrm{Al(CH_3)_3}$ is used to manufacture polyethylene.
(c) Iron catalysts are used in the Haber process for the production of ammonia.
(d) Polymerisation of alkynes is catalysed by palladium complexes.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is correct. $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ is used in the Contact process for the oxidation of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ to $\mathrm{SO_3}$.

Statement (b) is correct. A mixture of $\mathrm{TiCl_4}$ and $\mathrm{Al(CH_3)_3}$ (Ziegler-Natta catalyst) is used for the polymerisation of ethylene to polyethylene.

Statement (c) is correct. Finely divided iron is used as a catalyst in the Haber process to manufacture ammonia.

Statement (d) is incorrect. The polymerisation of alkynes is catalysed by nickel complexes, not palladium complexes. Palladium(II) chloride ($\mathrm{PdCl_2}$) is instead used in the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three
