questions.q: When potassium permanganate is heated at $513\text{ K}$, it decomposes to yield a major green-coloured compound. What is the change in the oxidation state of manganese and the corresponding change in magnetic behaviour from the reactant to this green product?
questions.solution:
Potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) on heating at $513\text{ K}$ decomposes as follows:

$2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{513\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

The reactant, $\text{KMnO}_4$, contains manganese in the $+7$ oxidation state. Its electronic configuration is $3d^0$, which has no unpaired electrons, making it diamagnetic.

The major green-coloured product is potassium manganate ($\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$). In this compound, manganese is in the $+6$ oxidation state. Its electronic configuration is $3d^1$, which contains one unpaired electron, making it paramagnetic.

Therefore, the oxidation state changes from $+7$ to $+6$, and the magnetic behaviour changes from diamagnetic to paramagnetic.

Answer: $+7$ to $+6$, diamagnetic to paramagnetic

The spin-only magnetic moment depends on the number of unpaired electrons ($n$), given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM. The ion with the maximum number of unpaired electrons will have the highest magnetic moment.

The electronic configurations of the given ions are:
$\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}$ (Z = 64): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{7}$ ($n = 7$)
$\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$ (Z = 63): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{6}$ ($n = 6$)
$\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ (Z = 58): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{1}$ ($n = 1$)
$\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ (Z = 71): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{14}$ ($n = 0$)

Since $\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}$ has the maximum number of unpaired electrons ($n = 7$), it exhibits the highest spin-only magnetic moment.

Answer: $\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ both exhibit a spin-only magnetic moment of zero.
Reason (R): Both ions lack unpaired electrons due to a completely filled $3d$ subshell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A): The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Cu}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^1$. Thus, $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^{10}$. It has 0 unpaired electrons, so its magnetic moment is zero.
The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Sc}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^1 4s^2$. Thus, $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^0$. It also has 0 unpaired electrons, so its magnetic moment is zero.
Therefore, the Assertion is true.

Reason (R): While $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ lacks unpaired electrons because of a completely filled $3d$ subshell ($3d^{10}$), $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ lacks unpaired electrons because it has an empty $3d$ subshell ($3d^0$).
Therefore, the Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Heating potassium permanganate produces a green solid (A). When an aqueous solution of (A) is treated with a dilute acid, it undergoes disproportionation to give a purple solution (B) and a brown-black precipitate (C). The oxidation states of manganese in compounds (B) and (C) are respectively:
questions.solution:
When potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) is heated, it decomposes to form potassium manganate, which is the green solid (A).

$2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 \text{ (A)} + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

In an acidic medium, the manganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$) undergoes a disproportionation reaction to form the permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$), which gives a purple solution (B), and manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$), which is a brown-black precipitate (C).

$3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- \text{ (B)} + \text{MnO}_2 \text{ (C)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The oxidation state of manganese in the purple solution (B), which contains the permanganate ion, is $+7$.

The oxidation state of manganese in the brown-black precipitate (C), which is $\text{MnO}_2$, is $+4$.

Thus, the oxidation states of manganese in (B) and (C) are $+7$ and $+4$ respectively.

Answer: $+7$ and $+4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ is widely used as a good analytical reagent in aqueous medium.
Reason (R): The oxidation of water by $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ is kinetically very slow.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ is widely used as a good analytical reagent in aqueous solutions.

Reason (R) is true and explains Assertion (A): The standard electrode potential for the $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}/\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ couple is $+1.74\text{ V}$, which indicates that thermodynamically it can oxidise water. However, the reaction rate is kinetically very slow. Because this oxidation of water is so slow, aqueous solutions of $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ are sufficiently stable to be used as analytical reagents.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following catalyst-reaction pairs is incorrectly matched?
options: Finely divided $\text{Ni}$ : Catalytic hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons
$\text{Zn}^{2+}$ : Oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate
questions.solution:
Transition metals and their compounds act as good catalysts due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and form complexes.

$\text{MnO}_2$ is used as a catalyst in the decomposition of $\text{KClO}_3$ to yield oxygen gas.

$\text{TiCl}_4$ with $\text{Al}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ forms the Ziegler-Natta catalyst, which is used for the polymerisation of ethene.

Finely divided $\text{Ni}$ is widely used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes).

The oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate is catalysed by $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, not $\text{Zn}^{2+}$. $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ has a completely filled d-orbital ($3d^{10}$) and a fixed +2 oxidation state, so it cannot provide the variable oxidation states required to catalyse this redox reaction.

Thus, the incorrectly matched pair is $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ : Oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate.

Answer: $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ : Oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion is :
questions.solution:
The atomic number of $\text{Co}$ is $27$.

The electronic configuration of a neutral $\text{Co}$ atom is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.

When forming the $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion, two electrons are removed from the outermost $4s$ orbital, giving the configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7$.

According to Hund's rule, filling the five degenerate $d$-orbitals with $7$ electrons results in $3$ unpaired electrons ($n = 3$).

The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

Substituting $n = 3$:
$\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $3.87$ BM

questions.q: When $\text{MnO}_2$ is fused with $\text{KOH}$ in the presence of an oxidising agent like $\text{KNO}_3$, a dark green coloured compound is formed. The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of the transition metal ion in this dark green compound is :
questions.solution:
The fusion of $\text{MnO}_2$ with $\text{KOH}$ and an oxidising agent like $\text{KNO}_3$ produces potassium manganate ($\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$), which is dark green in colour.

The oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in the manganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$) is $+6$.

The atomic number of $\text{Mn}$ is $25$.

Electronic configuration of neutral $\text{Mn}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.

Electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{6+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$.

Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 1$.

Spin-only magnetic moment, $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

$\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73 \text{ BM}$.

Note: Confusing the green manganate with the purple permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$, $\text{Mn}^{7+}$, $n=0$) leads to $0.00 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $1.73 \text{ BM}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Three different oxides of chromium, X, Y, and Z, exhibit the following properties:

Oxide X dissolves only in dilute acids.
Oxide Y dissolves in both acids and alkalies.
Oxide Z dissolves in water to give a strongly acidic solution.

The oxidation states of chromium in the oxides X, Y, and Z respectively are:
questions.solution:
The acid-base character of transition metal oxides depends on the oxidation state of the metal. Lower oxidation states form basic oxides, intermediate states form amphoteric oxides, and higher oxidation states form acidic oxides.

Oxide X dissolves only in dilute acids, which indicates it is a basic oxide. For chromium, the basic oxide is $CrO$, where the oxidation state of chromium is $+2$.

Oxide Y dissolves in both acids and alkalies, indicating it is an amphoteric oxide. The amphoteric oxide of chromium is $Cr_2O_3$, where the oxidation state is $+3$.

Oxide Z dissolves in water to give a strongly acidic solution, indicating it is an acidic oxide. The acidic oxide of chromium is $CrO_3$, where the oxidation state is $+6$.

Therefore, the oxidation states of chromium in X, Y, and Z are $+2$, $+3$, and $+6$ respectively.

Answer: $+2, +3, +6$

Hafnium does not contain $5f$ electrons, and the inert pair effect primarily applies to heavier p-block elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following transition metal oxides dissolves in both aqueous $\mathrm{HCl}$ and aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$?
questions.solution:
The ability of an oxide to dissolve in both aqueous acids (like $\mathrm{HCl}$) and aqueous alkalis (like $\mathrm{NaOH}$) indicates its amphoteric nature.

In transition metals, the acid-base character of oxides depends on the oxidation state of the metal. Lower oxidation states are generally basic, while higher oxidation states are acidic. Intermediate oxidation states often show amphoteric behaviour.

$\mathrm{V}_2\mathrm{O}_5$ is an amphoteric oxide (though mainly acidic). It dissolves in aqueous alkalis to give $\mathrm{VO}_4^{3-}$ salts and in acids to give $\mathrm{VO}_2^+$ salts.

$\mathrm{MnO}$ (oxidation state +2) is basic and dissolves only in acids.
$\mathrm{CrO}_3$ (+6) and $\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ (+7) are highly acidic oxides and dissolve only in alkalis.

Answer: $\mathrm{V}_2\mathrm{O}_5$

questions.q: Cerium (Z = 58) is an important member of the lanthanoid series. Which of the following correctly describes the magnetic nature and the chemical behaviour of the $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ ion in aqueous solution?
options: Paramagnetic and acts as a strong oxidising agent
Diamagnetic and acts as a strong reducing agent
Paramagnetic and acts as a strong reducing agent
Diamagnetic and acts as a strong oxidising agent
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of the Cerium atom (Z = 58) is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^1 5\mathrm{d}^1 6\mathrm{s}^2$.

The $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ ion is formed by the loss of all four valence electrons, resulting in the noble gas core configuration of $[\mathrm{Xe}]$. Since it has zero unpaired electrons, the $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ ion is diamagnetic.

The most stable oxidation state for lanthanoids is +3. Therefore, $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ has a strong tendency to gain one electron and revert to the more stable +3 state ($\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$).

Because it readily undergoes reduction, $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ acts as a strong oxidising agent in aqueous solutions.

Answer: Diamagnetic and acts as a strong oxidising agent

questions.q: A $3d$ series transition metal $\mathrm{M}$ exhibits an exceptionally high positive $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{M}^{3+} / \mathrm{M}^{2+}\right)$ value because its $\mathrm{M}^{2+}$ ion attains a stable half-filled $d$-subshell. The spin-only magnetic moment of the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ ion in aqueous solution is approximately:
questions.solution:
The metal $\mathrm{M}$ belongs to the $3d$ series. Its $\mathrm{M}^{2+}$ ion has a stable half-filled $d$-subshell, which means the electronic configuration of $\mathrm{M}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5$.

This identifies the metal $\mathrm{M}$ as Manganese ($\mathrm{Mn}$), which has a ground state configuration of $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.

The question asks for the spin-only magnetic moment of the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ ion ($\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$).

The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^4$.

The number of unpaired electrons ($n$) in $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is $4$.

The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is calculated as:
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90 \mathrm{BM}$.

Answer: $4.90 \mathrm{BM}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The absorption spectra of lanthanoid ions consist of sharp, narrow bands in the UV-visible region.

Statement II: The narrow bands are a result of strong interactions between $4f$ electrons and the surrounding ligand field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct because the electronic spectra of lanthanoid ions exhibit sharp, line-like narrow absorption bands primarily due to $f-f$ transitions.

Statement II is incorrect. The $4f$ orbitals in lanthanoids are deeply buried and effectively shielded by the outer $5s$ and $5p$ electrons. As a result, the $4f$ electrons interact very weakly with the surrounding ligand field. This weak interaction and shielding are precisely why the absorption bands remain narrow and sharp, unlike the broad bands seen in transition metals.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): On heating $\text{KMnO}_4$ at $513\text{ K}$, the major green-colored product obtained is paramagnetic in nature.
Reason (R): The thermal decomposition of $\text{KMnO}_4$ produces $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$, in which manganese is in the $+6$ oxidation state with one unpaired $d$-electron.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
When potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) is heated at $513\text{ K}$, it decomposes as follows:

$2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{513\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

The major green-colored product formed is potassium manganate ($\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$).

In $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$, the oxidation state of manganese is $+6$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{6+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$.

Since it contains one unpaired electron in its $d$-orbital, $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ is paramagnetic in nature. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

Reason (R) correctly identifies the green product as $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ and explains its paramagnetism based on the $+6$ oxidation state and the presence of one unpaired $d$-electron. Thus, Reason (R) is true and is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous divalent ion ($\mathrm{M}^{2+}$) of a $3d$ transition element exhibits a 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ BM}$. Which of the following statements correctly describes a property of the neutral element $\mathrm{M}$?
options: The neutral atom possesses an anomalous ground state electronic configuration of $3d^5 4s^1$.
The element exhibits a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ in its compounds.
The element belongs to group 8 of the modern periodic table.
The neutral atom has a completely filled $3d$ subshell.
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is given by $\sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.92 \text{ BM}$, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 5.92$, which gives $n = 5$.

The divalent ion $\mathrm{M}^{2+}$ belongs to the $3d$ series and has 5 unpaired electrons, so its outer electronic configuration must be $3d^5$.

The neutral atom $\mathrm{M}$ is formed by adding two electrons to the $4s$ orbital, giving the configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$. This corresponds to Manganese ($\mathrm{Mn}$).

Manganese belongs to group 7 and exhibits a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ (e.g., in $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$).

The configuration $3d^5 4s^1$ belongs to Chromium ($\mathrm{Cr}$). Group 8 corresponds to Iron ($\mathrm{Fe}$).

Answer: The element exhibits a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ in its compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following lanthanoid ions acts as a strong reducing agent and is also paramagnetic in nature?
questions.solution:
Lanthanoids predominantly show a $+3$ oxidation state. Ions in $+2$ or $+4$ oxidation states tend to convert to the stable $+3$ state, acting as reducing or oxidising agents respectively.

Let us evaluate the given ions:
$\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ (Z = 63): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{7}$. It readily loses one electron to form the stable $\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$ ($[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{6}$), acting as a strong reducing agent. It has $7$ unpaired electrons, making it highly paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$ (Z = 70): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{14}$. It acts as a reducing agent (converts to $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$), but has no unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic.
$\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ (Z = 58): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{0}$. It acts as an oxidising agent (converts to $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$) and is diamagnetic.
$\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ (Z = 71): $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{14}$. It is in the stable $+3$ state and is diamagnetic.

Therefore, $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ is the only ion that is both a strong reducing agent and paramagnetic.

Answer: $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following industrial processes:
(i) Oxidation of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ in the manufacture of sulphuric acid
(ii) Polymerisation of ethylene
(iii) Oxidation of ethyne to ethanal

Identify the correct sequence of the oxidation states of the transition metals present in the primary catalytic compounds used for the above processes respectively.
questions.solution:
(i) The catalyst used for the oxidation of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ in the manufacture of sulphuric acid (Contact process) is $\mathrm{V}_2\mathrm{O}_5$. The oxidation state of vanadium (V) in $\mathrm{V}_2\mathrm{O}_5$ is $+5$.

(ii) The catalyst used for the polymerisation of ethylene is the Ziegler-Natta catalyst, which is a mixture of $\mathrm{TiCl}_4$ and $\mathrm{Al(CH_3)_3}$. The transition metal is titanium (Ti), and its oxidation state in $\mathrm{TiCl}_4$ is $+4$.

(iii) The catalyst used for the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal is $\mathrm{PdCl}_2$. The oxidation state of palladium (Pd) in $\mathrm{PdCl}_2$ is $+2$.

Thus, the correct sequence of oxidation states is $+5, +4, +2$.

Answer: $+5, +4, +2$

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: It is a well-known fact that the $5f$ electrons shield the nuclear charge less effectively than the $4f$ electrons. Which of the following is a direct observable consequence of this poor shielding?
options: Lanthanoids show a greater element-to-element decrease in atomic size than actinoids.
The decrease in atomic size from element to element is greater in the actinoid series compared to the lanthanoid series.
Actinoids exhibit a smaller range of oxidation states than lanthanoids.
The $5f$ orbitals are more deeply buried in the atom than the $4f$ orbitals.
questions.solution:
The shielding effect of $5f$ electrons is poorer than that of $4f$ electrons. As a result, the effective nuclear charge experienced by the valence electrons increases more sharply from element to element in the actinoid series.

This causes a more pronounced actinoid contraction, meaning the decrease in atomic and ionic size from one element to the next is greater in actinoids than in lanthanoids.

Actinoids actually show a larger number of oxidation states because of the comparable energies of $5f$, $6d$ and $7s$ levels. Also, $4f$ orbitals are more deeply buried than $5f$ orbitals.

Answer: The decrease in atomic size from element to element is greater in the actinoid series compared to the lanthanoid series.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $V_2O_4$ dissolves in acids to give $VO^{2+}$ salts, whereas $V_2O_5$ dissolves in acids to give $VO_2^+$ salts.
Reason (R): Vanadium retains its $+4$ oxidation state in the $VO^{2+}$ ion and its $+5$ oxidation state in the $VO_2^+$ ion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct.
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. According to NCERT, $V_2O_4$ dissolves in acids to give $VO^{2+}$ (vanadyl) salts. On the other hand, $V_2O_5$ is an amphoteric oxide that dissolves in acids to give $VO_2^+$ (dioxovanadium) salts.

Reason (R) is also correct and explains the Assertion. The dissolution of these oxides in acids is a non-redox process. In $V_2O_4$, the oxidation state of vanadium is $+4$, which is retained in the $VO^{2+}$ ion (let the oxidation state be $x$, then $x - 2 = +2 \Rightarrow x = +4$). In $V_2O_5$, the oxidation state of vanadium is $+5$, which is retained in the $VO_2^+$ ion (let the oxidation state be $x$, then $x - 2(2) = +1 \Rightarrow x = +5$). Because the oxidation states are conserved, the two oxides form different oxocations in acidic medium.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Transition metal ions typically show broad absorption bands, whereas lanthanoid ions show sharp, narrow bands.

Reason (R): The $4f$ electrons in lanthanoids are highly exposed to the surrounding ligands, whereas the $(n-1)d$ electrons in transition metals are deeply buried and shielded.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. The absorption bands of transition metal ions are generally broad due to the strong interaction of their $d$-orbitals with ligands, whereas lanthanoid ions exhibit sharp, narrow bands due to $f-f$ transitions.

Reason (R) is false. The $4f$ electrons in lanthanoids are deeply buried and effectively shielded by the outer $5s$ and $5p$ subshells, leading to very weak interactions with the ligand field. In contrast, the $(n-1)d$ electrons in transition metals are outermost and highly exposed to the surrounding ligands, which causes their energy levels to split and broaden significantly.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of ions possesses the exact same number of unpaired electrons?
questions.solution:
The number of unpaired electrons is determined by writing the electronic configuration of each ion.

For $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ (Z = 25): The neutral atom is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^{5} 4\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Removing two electrons from the 4s orbital gives $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^{5}$, which has 5 unpaired electrons.

For $\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$ (Z = 62): The neutral atom is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{6} 6\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Removing three electrons (two from 6s, one from 4f) gives $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{5}$, which has 5 unpaired electrons.

Both $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$ have 5 unpaired electrons.

Evaluating the other options:
$\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ has 4 unpaired electrons ($3\mathrm{d}^{6}$), while $\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}$ has 7 unpaired electrons ($4\mathrm{f}^{7}$).
$\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ has 2 unpaired electrons ($3\mathrm{d}^{8}$), while $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ has 1 unpaired electron ($4\mathrm{f}^{1}$).
$\mathrm{V}^{3+}$ has 2 unpaired electrons ($3\mathrm{d}^{2}$), while $\mathrm{Nd}^{3+}$ has 3 unpaired electrons ($4\mathrm{f}^{3}$).

Answer: $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ (Z = 25) and $\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$ (Z = 62)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Copper(I) ion is unstable in aqueous solution and undergoes disproportionation to Copper(II) ion and solid copper.
Reason (R): Copper(II) ion has a more stable $3d^9$ electronic configuration compared to the completely filled $3d^{10}$ configuration of Copper(I) ion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. In aqueous solutions, $Cu^+$ undergoes disproportionation: $2Cu^+_{(aq)} \rightarrow Cu^{2+}_{(aq)} + Cu_{(s)}$.

Reason (R) is false. The $Cu^+$ ion has a completely filled $3d^{10}$ configuration, which is electronically more stable than the $3d^9$ configuration of $Cu^{2+}$. The instability of $Cu^+$ in aqueous solution is not due to its electronic configuration, but rather because the high negative hydration enthalpy of the $Cu^{2+}$ ion more than compensates for the second ionization enthalpy of copper.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.q: A transition metal $\text{M}$ belongs to the $3d$ series and possesses the highest melting point among the elements of this series. What is the spin-only magnetic moment of the $\text{M}^{3+}$ ion?
questions.solution:
In the $3d$ transition series, the melting point generally increases with the number of unpaired electrons, reaching a maximum at chromium ($\text{Cr}$), which has a $3d^{5} 4s^{1}$ configuration. (Manganese shows an anomalous dip and does not have the highest melting point).

Thus, the metal $\text{M}$ is Chromium ($\text{Cr}$).

The electronic configuration of $\text{Cr}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{5} 4s^{1}$.

The electronic configuration of the $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ion is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{3}$.

Number of unpaired electrons ($n$) = $3$.

The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is given by $\sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

$\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \text{ BM}$.

Choosing $\text{Mn}$ incorrectly as the metal with the highest melting point would lead to $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3d^{4}$), giving $4.90 \text{ BM}$. Calculating the magnetic moment for the neutral $\text{Cr}$ atom ($n=6$) would incorrectly give $6.93 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $3.87 \text{ BM}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Iron(III) acts as a catalyst in the reaction between iodide ion and persulphate ion.
Reason (R) : $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ catalyses the reaction by first oxidising persulphate ion to sulphate ion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. Iron(III) ions ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$) act as a catalyst in the reaction between iodide ion ($\text{I}^{-}$) and persulphate ion ($\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$).

Reason (R) is incorrect. In this catalytic cycle, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ does not oxidise persulphate ion. Instead, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ first oxidises iodide ion to iodine and gets reduced to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$. The $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ion is then oxidised back to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ by the persulphate ion, which itself gets reduced to sulphate ion.

The reactions involved are:
$2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{I}^{-} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{I}_2$
$2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{SO}_4^{2-}$

Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following periodic trends among transition elements is a direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction?
options: The atomic radii of 4d series elements are significantly larger than those of the corresponding 3d series elements.
The melting points of transition metals reach a maximum near the middle of each series.
The densities of 3d series elements are generally lower than those of the corresponding s-block elements.
The first ionization enthalpies of 5d series elements are generally higher than those of the corresponding 3d and 4d series elements.
questions.solution:
The lanthanoid contraction results in the 5d series elements having atomic radii very similar to those of the corresponding 4d series elements. However, the nuclear charge of 5d elements is higher by 32 units. Because the 4f electrons provide poor shielding, the effective nuclear charge acting on the outer valence electrons in 5d elements is significantly greater. As a result, the first ionization enthalpies of 5d elements are generally higher than those of the corresponding 3d and 4d elements.

Option 1 is true but is due to the addition of a new principal quantum shell.
Option 2 is true but is due to the maximum number of unpaired d-electrons contributing to strong metallic bonding.
Option 3 is a false statement; transition metals have higher densities than s-block elements.

Answer: The first ionization enthalpies of 5d series elements are generally higher than those of the corresponding 3d and 4d series elements.

questions.q:
Assertion : Cuprous ion $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{+}\right)$is colourless whereas cupric ion $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{++}\right)$is blue in the aqueous solution.
Reason : Cuprous ion $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{+}\right.$) has unpaired electrons while cupric ion $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{++}\right.$) does not.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Cuprous ions $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{+}\right)$is colourless because it has no unpaired electrons in the $3 d$ sub-shell as it has $3 d^{10}$ configuration. The cupric ion $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{++}\right)$has one unpaired electron as it has configuration $3 d^9$. By absorbing the visible light, the unpaired electron can migrate from one set of $d$-orbitals to another under the applied field of water molecules. Hence, cupric ion $\left(\mathrm{Cu}^{++}\right)$in aqueous solution shows blue colour.

Thus, Hs is a d-block element.

questions.q: Which of the following turns potassium dichromate paper green?
